prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously used naive substring/regex matching to find auth-param values (e.g. error, realm), which could produce false-positive matches against text inside other quoted parameter values. Both replace this with a proper quote-aware, comma-delimited tokenizer for the header's auth-params (handling escaped quotes and commas inside quoted strings). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing previously used naive substring/regex matching to find auth-param values (e.g. error, realm), which could produce false-positive matches against text inside other quoted parameter values. Both replace this with a proper quote-aware, comma-delimited tokenizer for the header's auth-params (handling escaped quotes and commas inside quoted strings). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both implement essentially the same quote/escape-aware comma-splitting algorithm, but #3041 goes a step further: its _split_www_authenticate_segments() splits the ENTIRE header on top-level commas (not just the portion after the first space), and _extract_bearer_auth_params() then explicitly walks the resulting segments to isolate only the Bearer scheme's auth-params, stopping when a different scheme token is encountered. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params() instead finds the first space in the header and treats everything after it as one flat list of auth-params, which does not correctly separate multiple challenges/schemes that can legally appear in a single WWW-Authenticate header value (RFC 7235 §4.1, e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer realm="y", error="z"'). #3041's approach handles a case #3012's does not.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same root cause in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): it JSON-decodes any string argument whose field annotation is not exactly `str`, which corrupts valid string values for `str | None`-style unions when the string happens to look like JSON (e.g. a stringified JSON payload passed to a `str | None` parameter). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same root cause in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): it JSON-decodes any string argument whose field annotation is not exactly `str`, which corrupts valid string values for `str | None`-style unions when the string happens to look like JSON (e.g. a stringified JSON payload passed to a `str | None` parameter). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032 generalizes the skip-condition to any union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, None}, but it checks raw type identity (`arg in _SIMPLE_TYPES`) without unwrapping `Annotated`, so it still misfires on `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` — the idiomatic FastMCP pattern for a described optional string parameter — leaving the bug unfixed for that common case. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip `Annotated[...]` before the union-member check, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly recognized as string-only and skipped. #3056's scope is narrower (only the two-member `str | None` shape vs. #2032's arbitrary simple-type unions), but it handles the annotation pattern MCP tool authors actually use, so it's the safer base to build on; #2032's broader union coverage (e.g. `str | int`) can be added on top in a follow-up.

clusters.pick_reason: Both implement essentially the same quote/escape-aware comma-splitting algorithm, but #3041 goes a step further: its _split_www_authenticate_segments() splits the ENTIRE header on top-level commas (not just the portion after the first space), and _extract_bearer_auth_params() then explicitly walks the resulting segments to isolate only the Bearer scheme's auth-params, stopping when a different scheme token is encountered. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params() instead finds the first space in the header and treats everything after it as one flat list of auth-params, which does not correctly separate multiple challenges/schemes that can legally appear in a single WWW-Authenticate header value (RFC 7235 §4.1, e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer realm="y", error="z"'). #3041's approach handles a case #3012's does not.

clusters.pick_reason: Both implement essentially the same quote/escape-aware comma-splitting algorithm, but #3041 goes a step further: its _split_www_authenticate_segments() splits the ENTIRE header on top-level commas (not just the portion after the first space), and _extract_bearer_auth_params() then explicitly walks the resulting segments to isolate only the Bearer scheme's auth-params, stopping when a different scheme token is encountered. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params() instead finds the first space in the header and treats everything after it as one flat list of auth-params, which does not correctly separate multiple challenges/schemes that can legally appear in a single WWW-Authenticate header value (RFC 7235 §4.1, e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer realm="y", error="z"'). #3041's approach handles a case #3012's does not.
